can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by a 'to'- infinitive.
example_raw:
I like to go to the zoo. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Arabic - Other; Pass)

Sometimes I don't like to go out because It's very cold. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Tagalog; Pass)

I want to invite you for dinner. (India; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Panjabi; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verb + to infinitive for intentions and preferences

positives: I want to go to the park.
She hopes to see you soon.
negatives: I want an apple right now.

example_raw:
I would like to meet you to give you some information about the Brannl State and the shops near her. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2008; Arabic - Other; Pass)

I'd like to invite you on Sunday about six o'clock in the evening. (Poland; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Polish; Pass)

positives: I would like to visit the museum.
She'd really like to join us.
negatives: I like to visit the museum.
I would love to join us.

can_do_statement: Can use 'like' followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.
example_raw:
I like to work with my teacher. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Italian; Pass)

I don't like to eat at College. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Italian; Pass)

I like reading lots of magazines. (Hungary; A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2010; Hungarian; Pass)

I don't like doing homework in college. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Thai; Pass)

I like learning grammar. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2007; Polish; Pass)

I like travelling by car. (A1 BREAKTHROUGH; 2011; Others; Pass)

positives: I like to read books.
He likes swimming in the ocean.

can_do_statement: Can use verbs expressing preference followed either by a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with no change in meaning.
example_raw:
I love to play football. (Thailand; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Thai; Pass)

I love to cook. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; French; Pass)

I prefer to play football but I often go to the gym. (A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Farsi; Pass)

I hate to watch any sports. (Poland; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2007; Polish; Pass)

I love cooking and also baking. (Mexico; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2004; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I love listening to music, especially hip-hop music. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

I hate wearing trousers in summer. (Spain; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Spanish - European; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: expressing strong preferences with interchangeable forms
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs of preference (love, hate, prefer) + to/ing

positives: I love to sing in the shower.
She hates waiting for the bus.

can_do_statement: Can use 'enjoy' followed by the '-ing' form.
example_raw:
We enjoy playing the piano and singing together. (Iran; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Farsi; Pass)

You know I really enjoy listening to music. (China; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2010; Chinese; Pass)

positives: I enjoy reading books at night.
She enjoys playing tennis.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would love to' followed by the 'to'-infinitive to give emphasis.
example_raw:
I'd love to do the concert. (France; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2005; French; Pass)

I'd love to hear it! (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

positives: I would love to see you tomorrow.
I'd really love to come along.
negatives: I love to see you tomorrow.
I would like to come along.

can_do_statement: Can use an increasing range of verbs followed by a 'to'-infinitive.
example_raw:
I bought them because I hope to go to England this year and the weather isn't very good. (Italy; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2008; Italian; Pass)

Please remember to bring your pyjamas and your tooth brush. (Cyprus; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2009; Greek; Pass)

Don't forget to come. (Iran; A2 WAYSTAGE; 2006; Farsi; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: expanding repertoire of verbs taking infinitives
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs (remember, forget, decide, plan) + to infinitive

positives: I forgot to call my mother.
They decided not to stay.

can_do_statement: Can use a wide range of verbs followed by a 'to-' infinitive.
example_raw:
… it's one of the reasons I decided to change class. (France; B1 THRESHOLD; 2002; French; Pass)

I'm going to buy pictures to hang on the wall, because my room seems to be very cold and very unfriendly. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2001; German; Pass)

ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs (seem, appear, tend, manage) + to infinitive

positives: It seems to be working perfectly.
She managed to finish the race.

can_do_statement: Can use a limited range of verbs followed by an '-ing' form.
example_raw:
I would like to stay there a few years to finish studying and to have my own money to start thinking of travelling. (Uruguay; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

So, would you mind telling Mr and Mrs Thomas. (China; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Chinese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: expanding repertoire of verbs taking gerunds
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs (finish, start, mind, keep, suggest) + ing

positives: I finished reading the novel.
Do you mind opening the window?

example_raw:
Let me know if it is suitable for you. (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Portuguese; Fail)

She makes me smile when I'm sad. (Yugoslavia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2010; Serbian; Pass)

She always makes me laugh! (Brazil; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Portuguese; Pass)

You are eighteen now, you can do what you want and they should let you do it. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

I think you should talk with your parents and try to make them understand how you feel and what you prefer. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

Maybe your parents are afraid of letting you go away by yourself, they still consider you their baby. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: causative and permissive verbs with bare infinitives

positives: She always makes me laugh.
They will let us enter early.
negatives: I made it to the party.

can_do_statement: Can use 'would prefer' + 'to' infinitive, often for politeness.
example_raw:
I would prefer to pay by cash. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2003; Pass)

I would prefer to meet you at six o'clock instead of four, at the café in my hometown. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

I'd prefer to go on holiday with my friends. (Germany; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; German; Pass)

positives: I would prefer to stay home tonight.
She'd clearly prefer to work alone.
negatives: I prefer to stay home tonight.
I would prefer a cup of tea.

can_do_statement: Can use 'help' + object + infinitive with or without 'to', with no change in meaning.
example_raw:
I wanted to help him to make some friends. He's just like me. (Turkey; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Turkish; Pass)

I hope that it will help you to keep fit. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Russian; Pass)

I hope my advice can help you choose where to go. (Italy; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Italian; Pass)

This house is terrible and I hope you can help me find something better. (B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Polish; Pass)

positives: Can you help me find my keys?
It helped them to understand better.

can_do_statement: Can introduce a new subject before the '-ing' form (using noun or object pronoun).
example_raw:
If your boss doesn't mind you delaying, it could be a possible solution. (Germany; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; German; Pass)

I could not stand people shouting at me, or taking pictures of me all day. It would be horrible. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

Oh just one more thing: would you mind me staying in your flat again? (Poland; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Polish; Pass)

We imagine it being a frozen land, where the people are ‘frozen’ too - both 'inside' and 'outside'. (Mexico; B2 VANTAGE; 1997; Russian; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: linking verbs to new subjects executing gerunds

positives: Do you mind me staying here?
I can't stand people shouting.
negatives: I can't stand the terrible shouting.

can_do_statement: Can use some verbs of requesting and commanding followed by a direct object and a 'to-'infinitive.
example_raw:
I would like you to come to a picnic on Saturday. (Argentina; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Spanish - Latin American; Pass)

I would like you to come to my office on 16th of May to discuss the terms of the contract. (Poland; B1 THRESHOLD; 2007; Polish; Pass)

Your parents want you to go on holiday with them this summer. (Russia; B1 THRESHOLD; 2008; Russian; Pass)

You asked me to tell you about one of my friends. (Greece; B1 THRESHOLD; 2009; Greek; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: verbs of commanding and requesting directed at an object
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs of requesting/commanding + object + to infinitive

positives: She asked him to leave immediately.
I want you to finish this task.

can_do_statement: Can follow some verbs with a 'to'-infinitive or an '-ing' form, with a change in meaning.
example_raw:
He said if you need to change the time, remember to contact him to make a new appointment. (Malaysia; B2 VANTAGE; 1999; Chinese; Pass)

I know it is difficult to get by with such a low salary but I am sure you have not stopped to think twice about your life. (Spain; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Spanish - European; Pass)

I remember feeling very unhappy and confused all day long. (Brazil; B2 VANTAGE; 1993; Portuguese; Pass)

After I had a baby, I needed to stop working. (Brazil; B2 VANTAGE; 2003; Portuguese; Pass)

ontology.mental_model: differentiating meaning based on verb complements (infinitive vs gerund)
ontology.pedagogical_hook: verbs that change meaning (remember, forget, stop) + to/ing

positives: I remembered to lock the door.
He stopped smoking last year.
